statement:
A **trie** (prefix tree) stores strings so that lookups by whole word or by prefix are fast. Implement the `Trie` class:

- `Trie()` creates an empty trie.
- `insert(word)` adds the string `word`.
- `search(word)` returns `true` if `word` has been inserted before, and `false` otherwise.
- `startsWith(prefix)` returns `true` if at least one inserted word begins with `prefix`, and `false` otherwise.

Input is given as parallel lists `ops` (method names) and `vals` (argument lists). The output lists each call's return value, with `null` for the constructor and for `insert`.

examples.explanation: `app` is only a prefix until it is inserted as a word itself.

why.d: Checks a sequence of 6 operations.

constraints: word and prefix consist only of lowercase English letters.
At most 3 * 10⁴ calls in total will be made to insert, search, and startsWith.
hints: `search` and `startsWith` walk the same path of characters; they only differ in what they require at the end of the walk.
Give each node a map (or 26-slot array) from character to child node, plus a boolean that marks the end of a complete word.
insert creates missing children along the path and sets the end flag on the last node; search requires the path to exist and the flag to be set; startsWith requires only that the path exists.

solutions.name: Brute Force (Check Every Word)
solutions.description: Test each word directly for starting with the prefix and count the matches.

code.python:
def countWordsWithPrefix(words, prefix):
    return sum(1 for w in words if w.startswith(prefix))
code.bash:
countWordsWithPrefix() {
    local -a words
    read -ra words <<< "$1"
    local prefix=$2 count=0 w
    for w in "${words[@]}"; do
        [[ $w == "$prefix"* ]] && (( count++ ))
    done
    echo "$count"
}

keyPoints: One startsWith check per word
Duplicates are counted separately
Empty prefix matches everything

solutions.name: Trie with Pass-Through Counts (Optimal)
solutions.description: Insert every word into a trie, incrementing a counter on each node passed; the counter at the node reached by walking the prefix is the answer.

code.bash:
countWordsWithPrefix() {
    local -a words
    read -ra words <<< "$1"
    local prefix=$2
    # Trie: node 0 is the root; child["node,ch"] = child node; pass[node] = words through it
    local -A child=()
    local -a pass=(0)
    local nodes=1 w node ch i
    for w in "${words[@]}"; do
        node=0
        (( pass[0]++ ))
        for (( i = 0; i < ${#w}; i++ )); do
            ch=${w:i:1}
            if [[ -z ${child[$node,$ch]+x} ]]; then
                child[$node,$ch]=$nodes
                pass[nodes]=0
                (( nodes++ ))
            fi
            node=${child[$node,$ch]}
            (( pass[node]++ ))
        done
    done
    # Walk the prefix; its node's count is the answer
    node=0
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#prefix}; i++ )); do
        ch=${prefix:i:1}
        if [[ -z ${child[$node,$ch]+x} ]]; then
            echo 0
            return
        fi
        node=${child[$node,$ch]}
    done
    echo "${pass[node]}"
}

keyPoints: Each trie node counts words passing through it
Root count = number of words (empty prefix)
Walk the prefix; falling off the trie means 0
Build once, query in O(p)

solutions.name: Brute Force (Try Each Prefix Length)
solutions.description: For each word, try its prefixes from shortest to longest and return the first one that no other word starts with; fall back to the whole word.

code.bash:
shortestUniquePrefix() {
    local -a words result=()
    read -ra words <<< "$1"
    local n=${#words[@]} i j len w p answer shared
    for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
        w=${words[i]}
        answer=$w
        for (( len = 1; len <= ${#w}; len++ )); do
            p=${w:0:len}
            # Is p also a prefix of some other word?
            shared=0
            for (( j = 0; j < n; j++ )); do
                if (( j != i )) && [[ ${words[j]} == "$p"* ]]; then
                    shared=1
                    break
                fi
            done
            if (( !shared )); then
                answer=$p
                break
            fi
        done
        result+=("$answer")
    done
    echo "${result[*]}"
}

keyPoints: Grow the prefix one letter at a time
Check it against every other word
Fallback: the whole word

solutions.name: Trie with Pass-Through Counts (Optimal)
solutions.description: Insert all words into a trie counting how many words pass through each node; a prefix is unique exactly at the first node with count 1.

code.bash:
shortestUniquePrefix() {
    local -a words result=()
    read -ra words <<< "$1"
    # Trie: node 0 is the root; child["node,ch"] = child node; pass[node] = words through it
    local -A child=()
    local -a pass=(0)
    local nodes=1 w node ch i answer
    for w in "${words[@]}"; do
        node=0
        for (( i = 0; i < ${#w}; i++ )); do
            ch=${w:i:1}
            if [[ -z ${child[$node,$ch]+x} ]]; then
                child[$node,$ch]=$nodes
                pass[nodes]=0
                (( nodes++ ))
            fi
            node=${child[$node,$ch]}
            (( pass[node]++ ))
        done
    done
    for w in "${words[@]}"; do
        node=0
        answer=$w
        # The first node only this word passes through ends the unique prefix
        for (( i = 0; i < ${#w}; i++ )); do
            node=${child[$node,${w:i:1}]}
            if (( pass[node] == 1 )); then
                answer=${w:0:i+1}
                break
            fi
        done
        result+=("$answer")
    done
    echo "${result[*]}"
}

keyPoints: Count words through every trie node
Count 1 means only this word has the prefix
Walk each word until the count drops to 1
No such node: keep the whole word

solutions.name: Brute Force (Compare Against Every Root)
solutions.description: For each sentence word, check every root with startsWith and keep the shortest root that matches.

code.bash:
replaceWords() {
    local -a dictionary words out=()
    read -ra dictionary <<< "$1"
    local sentence=$2
    read -ra words <<< "$sentence"
    local word best root
    for word in "${words[@]}"; do
        best=$word
        # Shortest root that starts this word
        for root in "${dictionary[@]}"; do
            if [[ $word == "$root"* ]] && (( ${#root} < ${#best} )); then
                best=$root
            fi
        done
        out+=("$best")
    done
    printf '%s\n' "${out[*]}"
}

keyPoints: Check every root for every word
Keep the shortest matching root
No match: keep the word

solutions.name: Trie of Roots, Shortest Match (Optimal)
solutions.description: Put all roots in a trie; walk each word through it and stop at the first node that ends a root, which is the shortest matching root.

code.bash:
replaceWords() {
    local -a dictionary words out=()
    read -ra dictionary <<< "$1"
    local sentence=$2
    read -ra words <<< "$sentence"
    # Trie: node 0 is the root; child["node,ch"] = child node; isEnd[node]=1 ends a root
    local -A child=()
    local -a isEnd=()
    local nodes=1 root node ch i word best
    for root in "${dictionary[@]}"; do
        node=0
        for (( i = 0; i < ${#root}; i++ )); do
            ch=${root:i:1}
            if [[ -z ${child[$node,$ch]+x} ]]; then
                child[$node,$ch]=$nodes
                (( nodes++ ))
            fi
            node=${child[$node,$ch]}
        done
        isEnd[node]=1
    done
    for word in "${words[@]}"; do
        # Walk the word; stop at the first end-of-root node
        best=$word
        node=0
        for (( i = 0; i < ${#word}; i++ )); do
            ch=${word:i:1}
            [[ -z ${child[$node,$ch]+x} ]] && break
            node=${child[$node,$ch]}
            if [[ -n ${isEnd[node]} ]]; then
                best=${word:0:i+1}
                break
            fi
        done
        out+=("$best")
    done
    printf '%s\n' "${out[*]}"
}

keyPoints: Trie stores every root once
Mark nodes that end a root
First end-mark on the walk = shortest root
Falling off the trie means no replacement
